VECTRA is a free, browser-based planning workspace for Mars, centred on Jezero Crater, where Perseverance landed. We built it for the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge. It combines NASA Mars Trek and USGS data in one place, with imagery, topography, thermal and mineral layers. Users can search 28 landing sites and named features, then draw routes, research stations and hazard zones on the map. The route tool reports distance and checks hazard overlap. An EVA planner takes the user’s own pace, time reserve and slope limit, plus an elevation profile, and a mission planner builds 1 to 7 sol schedules. Records log discoveries, rover requests and team missions.

It addresses the challenge by helping people prepare for survival and exploration on Mars. It makes terrain, hazards, time and slope visible before anyone sets foot there. It’s important because crewed missions are still years away, and students and planners need an accessible way to practise now. We kept every result clearly educational, not certified NASA crew standards.
details:
VECTRA is a public, browser-based planning workspace for Mars, centred on Jezero Crater, where Perseverance landed. It brings NASA Mars Trek and USGS data into one place, so users can explore the terrain and plan with it instead of switching between separate tools.

How it works: Users switch between 13 map layers: Viking, CTX and HiRISE imagery, MOLA topography and roughness, THEMIS and TES thermal layers, and TES mineral products. They can search 28 landing sites and named features, and click any point for coordinates and hazard screening. They can draw routes, research stations, hazard zones and mineral targets. The route tool reports great-circle distance and checks overlap with hazard zones. The EVA planner takes the user’s own walking pace, workload, available time, time reserve and slope threshold, plus an imported elevation profile (CSV), and returns an estimate. The Mission planner generates 1 to 7 sol schedules, and the Records section logs geological discoveries, rover support requests and two-astronaut team missions. Work can be imported and exported as GeoJSON, route CSV or a mission package, and it stays saved in the user’s own browser.

Benefits and intended impact: Human Mars missions are still years away, but planning starts now. VECTRA gives students, educators and aspiring mission planners a free, no-login way to practise reasoning about terrain, hazards, time and distance using real NASA data, preparing the next generation of explorers.

Tools: The web app is hosted on Netlify and uses NASA Mars Trek map layers and the USGS geological map. [Team: add your programming languages, map library, frameworks and design tools.]

Creativity: Our creative step is integration. Imagery, topography, thermal and mineral layers, route screening, EVA planning and mission records live in one workspace. We also made honesty a design feature: hazard zones are labelled illustrative, results are estimates from the user’s own inputs, and CRISM is linked to its archive instead of being faked as a live layer.

Factors we considered: Data accuracy and resolution limits, since only Jezero has high-resolution coverage. Avoiding overclaiming safety, since “within entered limits” is not a safety clearance. Accessibility, with no login or install. Privacy, since user data stays in the browser. Keeping it clearly educational, not certified NASA crew standards.
